newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros government bans Anjouan breakaway parties.
newsitem.headline: Comoros government bans Anjouan breakaway parties.

text.p: Comoro Islands Interior Minister Achirafi Said Hachim has banned two parties on Anjouan island, accusing them of working against the central government.
Hachim said in a statement late on Thursday the Organisation for Anjouan Independence (OPIA) and the Movement for Anjouan Separation (MSA) were "subversive organisations".
"Anyone who infringes the present order will be liable to legal penalties," he said in a statement broadcast on state radio.

The Indian Ocean archipelago, with a population of 190,000, became independent from France in 1975 and is ruled by President Mohamed Taki, but many Anjouan residents argue independence has only brought poverty and civil unrest.

The OPIA party wants Anjouan, Comoros' second island, to return to France, while the MSA, set up after clashes with the army last March and composed mainly of civil servants and students, wants independence.
Three people were killed on Anjouan on Monday and many others were wounded in clashes between secessionists and security forces, witnesses said.
